en: The Apadāna of the Elder Maṇipūjaka Kumuda Chapter 8.8 I was once a king named Sivi, and I gave a gift of a white elephant. Having performed that deed, I have now attained this state of being. I am now a monk who has reached the end of suffering. This is my final birth; there will be no further existence for me. This is my last body; I shall not take on another. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra, which is difficult to traverse. I have reached the further shore of the great flood. I have attained the supreme fruit of Arhatship. “Beside the Himalayas,
a river was flowing;
and along its banks,”
Then the Self-Existent One dwelt there,
having taken up his cross-legged seat,
which was well-disposed and delightful.
With a clear mind and joyful heart,
I offered [this] to the Buddha.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
The jewel that I offered;
I do not recognize any state of woe—
this is the fruit of worshiping the Buddha.
And in these twelve eons,
there were eight kings named Sataraṃsi.
Universal monarchs of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the venerable elder Maṇipūjaka recited these verses.
This is the eighth legend of the elder Maṇipūjaka.
